assertion_review.conditions_for_failure: max(gaps) > limit fails if the reading step is moved back to the tail of the pass or the pass bound stops clamping the steps, which is what the recorded red log shows at the base ordering (18.3s against 8s); the count assertion fails if a pass publishes nothing; accepted['utc'] == published.readings[-1]['utc'] fails if the reader parses a different record than the watcher saw.
assertion_review.independence: The separations are read from the readings' own timestamps, not from the values handed to the sampler; the limit comes from the reader (supervisor.node_disk_sample_max_age_seconds) rather than a literal in the assertion, and :246 checks that reader resolves the configured value.
assertion_review.limit: The scaled margin is 6 seconds of wait plus pass bound against an 8-second limit on one machine, so a much slower host shrinks the headroom without changing the ordering under test.

assertion_review.conditions_for_failure: published['sampler_pid'] == first.pid fails if the sampler stops exporting FLEET_HEALTH_SAMPLER_PID (the recorded red log shows the base arm failing with KeyError: 'sampler_pid'); the replacement wait fails if the lock is not released after the group dies; the separation assertion fails if a replacement restarts a long wait before publishing.
assertion_review.independence: Both pids are the operating system's pids of processes the test started, not values the test hands to the code.
assertion_review.limit: The separation is measured from two readings of one record file, so a replacement that published to a different state directory would fail the pid wait rather than the separation.

assertion_review.conditions_for_failure: The reason assertions fail if sampler_pid is dropped from NodeDiskSampleError or from node_disk_reading_obligation; the age assertions fail if age_seconds stops being carried; _blocking_items([row]) == [] fails if node-disk-stale leaves the hook's non-blocking set, and == [pressure] fails if the low-space row is wrongly exempted.
assertion_review.independence: The pid is a live process the test started but it is written into the fixture reading rather than produced by a sampler; the blocking assertions are independent of the row's text because _row_is_actionable reads only the kind, and the pressure row is the positive control that the predicate still returns something.
assertion_review.limit: The case never drives the obligations view itself, so a view that dropped node-disk rows before calling _blocking_items would not be caught here.

findings.disposition_hint: give the sweep its own bound outside pass_end, as the reading step has, or run it on a pass of its own
findings.text: non-blocking: reclaim-node-scratch runs last and bounded() returns 124 as soon as the pass budget is spent (bin/fleet-health:117-118), while the nine steps ahead of it can each consume their bound — the plan's own measurement has seven 20-second steps against a 90-second pass, so on a loaded node the sweep never runs and unowned scratch is never reclaimed, where the base at least reclaimed whatever it managed inside its 15-second disk bound.

findings.disposition_hint: add the three kinds to NON_BLOCKING_DUTY_KINDS, or have the mirror derive from the constants
findings.text: non-blocking: the hook's _NON_BLOCKING_KINDS documents itself as mirroring the derivation's own vocabulary, and the change added node-disk-stale, node-disk-missing and node-disk-unreadable only to the copy at reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:268-270; NON_BLOCKING_DUTY_KINDS still omits all three, so the two sets now disagree and any consumer that reads the owner treats a stale disk reading as a blocking duty.
